html:
Castle Bravo was a US hydrogen bomb test at Bikini Atoll on 1 March 1954, the largest nuclear blast the United States ever set off. It was far bigger than its makers expected.

Fallout snowed down on the people of Rongelap and Utirik atolls, who were evacuated only days later; many suffered burns and later cancers. It also fell on a Japanese fishing boat, the Lucky Dragon, whose crew fell ill, causing outrage in Japan.

Rongelap was declared safe and resettled in 1957, but its people left again in 1985, with the help of Greenpeace's Rainbow Warrior. Bravo fed the global campaign that led to the 1963 test ban treaty. See Bikini.
